audit_findings.title: The full June 30 cash balance may not be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $958.706 million maximum bridge exposure; $7.53/share; 9.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash separately to equity value; any cash required for seasonal operations should be excluded as excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, we normally require the use of cash to fund losses and working capital needs, periodically resulting in a working capital deficit, from May through January.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates seasonal liquidity needs, but does not establish how much of June cash is operational. Even the conservative upper bound of removing all $958.706 million lowers base value from $83.50 to about $75.97/share and the 30% buy-below level from $58.45 to about $53.18, still above the $49.06 price. Thus this can materially alter the value estimate but not the stated base-case purchase conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain monthly cash, seasonal CLOC usage, covenant headroom and minimum-liquidity data; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Existing uncertain-tax obligations may require an equity bridge deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $163.961 million gross upper-bound reference ($136.161 million unrecognized tax benefits plus $27.8 million accrued interest); $1.29/share; 1.54% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement of previously accrued tax positions could require a one-time equity bridge deduction because payment may not reduce forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Included in the total gross unrecognized tax benefit ending balance as of June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024 are $ 120.5 million, $ 232.8 million and $ 207.5 million respectively, which if recognized, would impact our effective tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: A possible bridge omission exists, but settlement is not demonstrated and the filed gross amounts exceed any expected payment net of offsets. Even deducting the full $163.961 million would reduce base value by only about $1.29/share and the buy-below level by about $0.90/share, far less than the $9.39 gap between buy-below and market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the tax reserves and accrued interest to the balance sheet, estimate settlement cash net of tax assets and expirations, and rerun only if an amount is not already captured in OE or working capital.

audit_findings.title: Sand Canyon creates an unbounded legacy claim outside continuing operations
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (companywide litigation accrual is $18.4 million; no Sand Canyon allocation or bound is filed)
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued legacy mortgage claims could require a direct equity bridge deduction; recurring discontinued-operation losses could also reduce OE if excluded from the historical series.
audit_findings.evidence: The creditors of SCC or other potential claimants may attempt to assert claims against us for payment of SCC's obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that parent-level claims may be asserted and that some exposures cannot be estimated, but it does not demonstrate an additional loss or quantify Sand Canyon's share of the $18.4 million accrual. Estimable losses above accrual are described as immaterial, while unestimable exposure remains open; therefore the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Trace discontinued-operation cash losses through every OE year and obtain claim-level accruals, asserted damages, parent guarantees, indemnities, insurance coverage and limitation periods before deciding whether to deduct an additional equity claim.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration may be an omitted claim on cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.6 million maximum combined liability; $0.21/share; 0.25% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Purchase consideration not passing through future earnings belongs in the equity bridge, while employment compensation should remain in OE and must not also be deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: Liabilities related to acquisitions for (1) estimated contingent consideration based on expected financial performance of the acquired business and economic conditions at the time of acquisition and (2) estimated accrued compensation related to continued employment of key employees were $ 26.6 million and $ 29.6 million as of June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, with amounts recorded in deferred revenue and other liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms a $26.6 million combined liability but does not split purchase consideration from compensation. Even treating the entire balance as an omitted bridge claim would reduce base value by only about $0.21/share and the buy-below level by about $0.15/share, which cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the liability split and payment schedule, trace compensation through projected OE, and deduct only purchase consideration not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth depends on pricing and acquisition economics despite flat total volume
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed sensitivity: base-to-bear reduction of $1.924 billion or $15.10/share; bull-to-bear reduction of $3.051 billion or $23.95/share
audit_findings.mechanism: Organic volume, pricing, mix and acquisition returns determine forecast OE growth; acquisition spending needed to sustain growth must remain deducted from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended June 30, 2026 our total assisted tax return volume, which includes both company-owned and franchise offices, decreased 0.1% from the prior year due to a decrease in franchise tax return volumes, partially offset by an increase in company-owned tax return volumes.
audit_findings.explanation: Flat total assisted volume does not prove the 4% or 6% OE growth assumptions are erroneous, because pricing, mix and other businesses can still grow OE. Materiality is nevertheless demonstrated by the supplied scenarios: moving from 4% base growth to 0% reduces value from $83.50 to $68.40/share, and the bear-case 30% buy-below level is about $47.88, below the $49.06 market price. The unresolved growth composition can therefore change the purchase conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical OE growth into organic volume, price, channel mix, Wave and acquired-office contributions; include recurring acquisition cash requirements, then rerun growth cases supported by that decomposition.

audit_findings.title: A post-year-end restructuring charge is absent from FY2026 OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.3 million pre-tax; $0.065/share before tax; 0.078% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The announced severance payment is a one-time post-balance-sheet cash claim that could be deducted in the bridge or incorporated into near-term OE, but not both.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to execute the workforce reduction by the end of the fiscal quarter ending September 30, 2026, and we expect to incur an estimated pre-tax charge associated with severance and related costs under the program of $8.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission from FY2026 is demonstrated, although whether normalized anchor OE should include the nonrecurring charge depends on the treatment of related savings. A dollar-for-dollar deduction would reduce base value by only about $0.07/share and the buy-below level by about $0.05/share, far too little to change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the actual cash charge, applicable tax benefit and recurring savings; reflect the net one-time claim once in a rerun and avoid double-counting it in OE.
